name: IETF vcon (Virtualized Conversations WG)
status: Active working group in the Applications and Real-Time Area, charter-ietf-vcon-01 approved (last updated 2026-03-18); its core draft, draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core (Standards Track), is at revision -05, published on 2026-10-31 (datatracker, read 2026-11-09; -04 was dated 2026-09-07). The datatracker lists four charter milestones, dated 2023-12-31 (adopt two drafts) and 2024-06-30 (submit them to the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG)), and shows no completion state. The virtual interim of 2026-10-08 (14:00 to 16:00 UTC) was held; the editor's message after it is quoted below. Minutes of that interim: not found in the latest 40 messages of the vcon list (to 2026-10-11), read 2026-10-13; the datatracker interim materials were not read. On 2026-10-23 the datatracker still shows draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 as the current revision and charter-ietf-vcon-01 as approved, and the history of the charter has no entry after 2026-03-18. The virtual interim of 2026-10-22 (interim-2026-vcon-05) was held: its agenda, slides, bluesheets, recording and chat log are on the datatracker, and no minutes were published there on 2026-10-23. Recharter state, 2026-10-13: the datatracker history of the charter shows no revision after charter-ietf-vcon-01 (last action 2026-03-18, a change of Area Director); the recharter text exists only in the repository file changed by PR #37 (merged 2026-10-08) and is not an approved charter. PR #41 on that file had no comments on 2026-10-13; on 2026-10-22, after the interim, it was changed by commit eb8269f, "Remove instructions and approvals, per the 2026-10-22 interim", and it now adds to the AI Agent Extension "references to records in other systems that resulted from the conversation, such as an order or a payment" and the use case "Agent-Mediated Transactions, such as Purchases"; it was merged into main on 2026-10-25 at 03:12 UTC by dgpetrie (merge commit 8e61484), with no comments or reviews, and the merged text is that of commit eb8269f; a later commit on main, 2bcddb9 (2026-10-25, 03:19 UTC, by dgpetrie), removed the limit to a single extension ("Define an extension" became "Define one or more extensions") and fixed a spelling mistake, and left the two phrases above as they were. On 2026-10-25 the datatracker still gives charter-ietf-vcon-01 as the latest revision of the charter (state Approved, new revision of 2023-12-02), its latest event is the change of Area Director of 2026-03-18, and no revision follows -01. Issue #40 of the core draft repository (opened 2026-10-10 by a participant, no comments) quotes section 2.4 of -04, "Objects that refer to a file which is externally stored from the vCon MUST have the parameters: url, content_hash", and says that references to a streaming-service page or to a recording behind a login cannot be hashed; it reports, as its own measurement on a public dataset, that 4,079 of 8,181 containers fail the schema on that one finding (a figure declared by the issue author, not re-run here).
relevance: The charter defines vCon as a JSON container "to contain and/or reference conversational data, including call style metadata, recordings, data exchanged or presented in the conversations, conversation analysis, transcriptions, translations and annotations", so it is the IETF format for the record of a conversation. On 2026-10-06 a participant proposed on the list to recharter the group to finish the core specification and to add an extension for "ai agent interaction record data"; the charter text he points to adds a baseline format and an "AI Agent Extension" for tool call requests and responses, model details, token usage, prompts and reasoning. The AUDIT effort proposes to treat VCON as its record format for interaction records (see ietf-audit); a related individual draft, draft-rosenberg-cheq-00 (dated 2025-07-24, expiry date 2026-01-25), defines a signed object by which a human confirms an action proposed by an AI agent. On 2026-10-06 the author of this map asked on the list whether the extension's list could name "user instructions and approvals, and references to related records in other protocols"; no reply to that message is among the 6 list messages of 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07 that were read. On 2026-10-07 the editor of the core draft reported an updated editors copy with "elevation of the party_history events to the top level Events Object" and a Session concept, and that the examples are not yet updated. The editor of the core draft wrote on 2026-10-08, "After discussion in the vCon Interim WG Meeting today, this PR has been merged in to the Charter in the repo."; pull request #37 shows the merge at 15:53 UTC (merge commit 5bd8dbf, file vcon_charter.md in ietf-wg-vcon/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core). This is a change to the working group's charter file in its repository; no IESG action on a new charter was found. Pull request #39, a typo fix to the charter, was reported merged on the list on 2026-10-08. The individual draft draft-birkholz-vcon-ai-agent-extension-00 (Standards Track; Birkholz, Petrie, McCarthy-Howe, Rosenberg, Steele; published on the datatracker on 2026-11-02 at 23:29 UTC, 2026-11-03 in Rome) defines the vCon extension `ai_agent` for agent metadata, tool invocations, reasoning traces and system events, and calls itself "a replacement for the former Verifiable Agent Conversation Records specification"; its section 8.5 says that the signed form gives "authenticity and integrity, not non-repudiation", and section 8.6 that "an agent that controls its own recording can omit or falsify entries". The words approval, consent, delegation, mandate, purchase, checkout and commerce do not occur in its text, and payment occurs only in references to PCI DSS (read 2026-11-09).
